findings.title: Restore rejection of zero-length suffix ranges
findings.body: Removing the zero check makes `bytes=-0` (and `bytes=-00`) parse as `(0, None)`, indistinguishable from `bytes=0-`. For a nonempty resource, `Response.make_conditional(..., accept_ranges=True)` consequently returns the entire body with status 206 instead of rejecting the unsatisfiable suffix with 416. Restore the guard before assigning `end = None`. Verified at both revisions using `/workspace/.venv/bin/python -` with a reproduction calling `parse_range_header` and `make_conditional` on a ten-byte response: head returned `206`, `Content-Range: bytes 0-9/10`, and all ten bytes; base rejected both zero-suffix forms with 416. Ordinary `bytes=-1` and `bytes=0-` behaved identically at both revisions.

findings.title: Respect morphIgnore when copying settle attributes
findings.body: When morphIgnore includes `style`, an innerHTML swap containing a matching ID now permanently retains the old element’s style. This loop unconditionally copies the old style, but the restore task still uses __copyAttributes, which skips attributes matching morphIgnore. Previously both steps respected that setting. Running `node /workspace/crow-settle.mjs` on both revisions with morphIgnore set to `['data-htmx-powered', 'style']` and a red-to-green replacement produced `color:green` at base and `color:red` at head after awaiting the swap; screenshots confirm the difference. Apply consistent attribute filtering during copying and restoration so ignored attributes cannot become stuck at their old values.
